sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the seemingly negative expressions in the blessings of Bechukosai are actually lofty blessings from the level of the Hidden, as interpreted by the Tzemach Tzedek, and this empowers each Jew to reveal goodness openly.

translations.translation: A)
And in particular, this already occurred in previous generations,
and a great deed,
as related in the Gemara,
that they said expressions that appear externally [negative] etc., but in truth they are all blessings,
and that they blessed him with such language is as the Tzemach Tzedek explained,
because a blessing in this manner is from the aspect of the Hidden,
for blessings from the aspect of the Hidden are more exalted blessings, and also their drawing down below is with greater force
(with a storm).
And as it is stated in the Gemara there,
that they blessed him "you will bear children" etc., the drawing down and revelation of the power of Ein Sof,
"in a generation of the upright He will be blessed."
And this explanation
(that they blessed him with such language because a blessing in this manner is from the aspect of the Hidden)
the Tzemach Tzedek says "appears more as its simple meaning."
For before this, it is brought there
(regarding the blessings in the portion of Bechukosai)
that it is the opposite of blessing, but this refers to the opposite side.
And afterwards he brings a more elevated explanation,
that the blessings were said in such language in order to sharpen [the intellect].
For even according to this explanation,
the matter of the blessing in this language is not in simplicity and revelation,
since in order to grasp the true essence of the matter, one needs sharpening of the intellect.
But afterwards he concludes,
that the blessings were said in such language not because of a deficiency, G-d forbid, but rather because the blessings are more exalted.
And about this explanation he says that it "appears more as its simple meaning,"
for that these expressions are blessings is not a sharpened explanation but rather the simple explanation,
even in the world of simplicity.
And after the Tzemach Tzedek opened the way,
and especially that he taught and gave this as Torah from the language of instruction,
this became an instruction and empowerment for each and every one,
to explain and reveal the blessing even in expressions and matters that in their externality appear etc.,
and on the contrary,
these blessings are the most exalted,
and according to their simple meaning,
in the revealed and manifest good.
For this power
(to draw down all matters in the revealed and manifest good)
is also throughout all the days of the year.
And especially on Rosh Hashanah when they crown the King with great joy
(as brought above from my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe),
for joy breaks all boundaries.
And all the more so on the festival of Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat,
for all the effluences made through the shofar blast are made on Shabbat of itself,
for on Shabbat the aspect of simple delight is drawn down,
as explained at length in the discourse "Yom Tov Shel Rosh Hashanah Shechal Liyot B'Shabbat" of the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the phrase "Adon Olam" refers to the absolute will in Atzmus, and through the service of Rosh Hashanah, Jews draw down from this level into physical matters, resulting in salvation and the true redemption.

translations.translation: B)
And this is "Adon Olam, who reigned before any creature was created,"
and my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, explains in his discourse on this topic
(as brought above at the beginning of the discourse)
that "Adon Olam" in gematria equals "Ein Sof," referring to Malchus as it is in His Essence,
the absolute will in His Essence,
and he explains there,
that regarding the absolute will in His Essence, the arousal of the feminine waters does not apply at all.
But nevertheless,
all this and the discourse "Adon Olam" comes
(as above)
in continuation of the discourse "Yom Tov Shel Rosh Hashanah Shechal Liyot B'Shabbat," which explains the matter of the shofar blast on Rosh Hashanah
(the service that includes all the particular services of the entire year),
that the service of Israel effects not only the building of Zeir Anpin
(and also all the levels and partzufim of all the chain of descent,
as above at length),
and not only does it arouse in the Ein Sof before the contraction the aspect of the revealed will
(in the aspect of revelation to another)
and also the aspect of the hidden will
(in the aspect of revelation to Himself),
but beyond this,
that because Israel are rooted in Atzmus,
they draw down also from the aspect of the absolute will in His Essence,
the aspect of "Adon Olam" in gematria "Ein Sof."
And this drawing down is
(primarily)
below in the physical world of action,
and within this itself—in physical matters,
for in addition to the judgment on Rosh Hashanah regarding the drawing down of Divinity,
"judgment"
"for the G-d of Yaakov,"
the primary judgment on Rosh Hashanah is regarding physical influences,
and Israel prevail in the judgment in both matters,
both in spiritual influences and in physical influences—in children, life, and ample sustenance,
and as stated, the primary matter of Rosh Hashanah is the drawing down into physicality,
"He works salvations in the midst of the earth,"
for the drawing down of salvations
(in all the interpretations thereof)
will be in a manner of "activity,"
for the term "activity" indicates specifically a physical action, even more than the term "making,"
and within this itself, "in the midst of the earth,"
in the lowest level, beneath which there is no lower level.
And simply put,
each and every Jew is written and sealed in the book of the completely righteous,
for "Your people are all righteous"
(completely righteous),
immediately for life,
and immediately for redemption,
for each and every Jew will go out from exile to the true and complete redemption,
and as it is stated in the haftarah of Rosh Hashanah,
"a great congregation shall return here,"
for in this is included every single Jew, as explained at length in the haftarah of Rosh Hashanah,
and with great joy,
and as above, that the coronation of the King is with great joy,
and "everlasting joy upon their heads,"
in the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach,
speedily, literally.
